title.text: Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center (Crocodile Farm)

title_en.text: Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center (Crocodile Farm)

tagline.text: A crocodile farm south of Puerto Princesa that protects the Philippine crocodile

location.label: Location
location.text: Along the national road in Barangay Irawan, south of Puerto Princesa City, Palawan

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: About 1 hour (30 minutes–1 hour if added to a city tour)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Listed centre admission ₱100 adults, ₱80 children, ₱90 seniors. Check transport and optional tours separately

children.text: This crocodile farm and wildlife rescue center lies about a 30-minute drive south of Puerto Princesa city center. It was founded in 1987 to breed the critically endangered Philippine crocodile, and you can see everything from hatchlings to adults in one stop, which makes it a good short visit with children.
The Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center is better known locally simply as the "Crocodile Farm." From Puerto Princesa city center, drive south along the national road for
about 30 minutes

to reach Barangay Irawan, and the center sits right beside the road. According to Wikipedia, it opened on August 20, 1987 as the Crocodile Farming Institute and took its current name in 2000. It is also known to have begun as a joint project of the Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).

The grounds cover about 10 hectares, and records show that in October 2021 the facility held 1,450 crocodiles and 245 other wild animals, 1,695 animals in all. The crocodiles you see here fall into two main kinds. One is the Philippine crocodile (Crocodylus mindorensis), found only in the Philippines. The other is the saltwater crocodile (Crocodylus porosus), which also lives in Palawan's rivers and mangroves. The Philippine crocodile is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, and one estimate puts fewer than 150 mature adults left in the wild. The center breeds these crocodiles in captivity and rescues and cares for injured wildlife.

To a traveler it looks something like a zoo, but the feel is different. Enclosures follow the animals' growth stage by stage: tanks of newly hatched young, pens for mid-sized crocodiles, and ponds for adults several meters long. Besides crocodiles, you can see rescued birds, monkeys and other animals. Guided tours explain how to tell Philippine crocodiles from saltwater crocodiles and why they need protection. Water can pool on the ground in front of the hatchling tanks, so watch your step to keep your shoes dry. Adult crocodiles often barely move during the day and rest by the water with their mouths open. This is natural body-temperature regulation, so do not mistake it for illness or death.

It is a good choice when you have some spare time in Puerto Princesa beyond the Underground River, or when you want a short outing with children on a rainy day. Go expecting a visit to a conservation facility rather than a flashy show, and you are more likely to be satisfied. Conditions and open areas can change with the season, so check the latest announcements before you go. Some visitors feel uneasy that this is a facility that breeds crocodiles. The center is known to raise saltwater crocodiles partly for the leather trade, but keep in mind that the Philippine crocodile is a protected species whose trade is prohibited.

The Philippine crocodile is one of the most threatened crocodiles on Earth. The center has bred this species in captivity since 1987, and it is one of the few places in Palawan where you can see it up close. Wild populations remain mainly in northern Luzon and southwestern Mindanao. The species is now protected under Philippine law, and trade in it is prohibited.

Pens are divided by growth stage, from tanks holding freshly hatched young to large ponds for adult crocodiles. You can see in one walk how much the same species changes as it grows, which makes it easy to explain to children.

Wild saltwater crocodiles live in small numbers in some Palawan river mouths and around Balabac. At the center you can see them from a safe distance. Stay back from the railing in front of the larger animals.
Besides crocodiles, the center is said to hold rescued birds, monkeys and peacocks. The animals change depending on rescue cases, so ask the staff at the entrance what is on view.
The
centre booking page
lists admission and optional guided routes. Confirm available routes and the start time for your visit.
A local guide advises that the animals are most active at feeding time. There is no reliable published schedule, so ask the staff when you arrive and plan your visit around it.
The center is known to have four parts: crocodile farming research, wildlife rescue, an ecological destination park and a training center. The visitor area is only a portion of these.

items.title: A half day from the city
items.subtitle: Crocodile farm and a look at the Iwahig River

children.text: Leave Puerto Princesa city center. By private car or a chartered tricycle, the center takes about 30 minutes. Check the schedule locally.
Arrive at the center and buy your ticket. Going early means the crocodiles are more active and you can visit quietly before tour buses arrive.
Walk through with a guide, from the hatchling tanks to the adult crocodile ponds. Listen to the explanations and take photos along the way.
See the rescued birds and other animal enclosures, then browse the souvenirs near the exit.
Ask about a paddle boat ride on the nearby Iwahig River. A local guide recommends it as a hidden gem. Check locally whether it is running.
Head back to the city for lunch. A seafood restaurant near the Baywalk is a safe choice.
This is an example, not a fixed route. Open areas and tour times vary with conditions on the day.

items.title: Combined with a city tour
items.subtitle: City sights and a half-day schedule

children.text: Board your Puerto Princesa city tour vehicle. Most city tours include the crocodile farm, so you do not need separate transport.
Spend about
30 minutes–1 hour
at the crocodile farm.
Move on to the other stops on the tour, such as the Baywalk and Plaza Cuartel in the city.
Tour contents differ by operator. Be sure to ask when booking whether the crocodile farm is included.
Several airlines fly nonstop from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS). Check the airline's notices for flight time and schedule.
The airport is close to the city, so it is easy to reach your hotel in town by tricycle or taxi. Negotiate the fare locally or check the meter.

items.title: From the city to the center

children.text: The center is on the national road in Barangay Irawan,
about 30 minutes
south of the city. A private car or chartered tricycle is the most convenient way.
The
Puerto Princesa tourism office

lists Irawan jeepneys or multicabs on the highway at ₱25 per person and tricycles from the airport or city at ₱300 per vehicle for up to three passengers. Check fares and the return ride before boarding.
A half-day city tour may substitute the butterfly garden for the centre. Confirm the actual stop before booking.
Return transport can be hard to find here, so a chartered vehicle or a tour is easier.

The center is open year-round, but most of the visit is outdoors, so the dry season (December–May) is more comfortable. In the rainy season paths can be slippery and ponds can swell, so bring an umbrella and sandals.
Early morning is best. You avoid the midday heat, and one guide says crocodiles are more active in the morning. Timing your visit with feeding time lets you see livelier behavior.

There is almost no lodging around the center, so most visitors stay at a hotel or guesthouse in Puerto Princesa and make a day trip. The city offers many options, including hotels near the airport and mid-range hotels near the Baywalk. It is a good light stop on the afternoon you arrive or the day before your Underground River trip. Since the airport is close to the city, you can see the crocodile farm on the afternoon you arrive and go to the Underground River the next morning, which makes the travel efficient.

It is better to eat in the city. There are restaurants around the center, but the choice is narrow. Palawan seafood is fresh, so have dinner around the city Baywalk and bring only light snacks and water to the center. If you miss Korean food or coffee, look in the central part of the city. Businesses open and close often, so check on a map app.
Go early in the morning, when the crocodiles are more active and tour groups are smaller.
Ask at the entrance for today's feeding time and when the guided tour starts. Timing your visit with feeding time makes the animals move more.
If you bring children, make sure they never put their hands inside the railings.
There are sunny stretches with little shade, so you need a hat, sunscreen and water.
It is often part of Puerto Princesa city tours, so decide first whether to join a tour or go on your own.
Carry cash in pesos. Entrance fees and souvenirs are often paid in cash.
Pairing it with a paddle boat ride on the nearby Iwahig River or a firefly tour makes for a fuller half day.
Noting the crocodiles and species names you see gives you something to talk about with your children.
Use the
centre booking page
to review admission and optional routes. Contact the centre at +63 995 033 8967 about opening times for a particular date or a group visit.
Crocodiles are extremely dangerous. Do not put your hands or objects inside the railings.
Feed animals only when staff direct you to, and never throw food on your own.
Avoid flash photography and loud noises, which can startle the animals.
Confirm the visit time and open areas before booking a group or city tour.
Floors are slippery when it rains. Non-slip shoes are safer than flip-flops.
A world-famous attraction that takes a long drive north of the center. It is usually done as a separate full-day trip.
A city with lodging, restaurants and the airport. The crocodile farm is
about 30 minutes
south of the city.
A seaside promenade visited together with the crocodile farm on city tours. Good for dinner and watching the sunset.
A popular island-hopping destination close to the city. Doing it on the same day as the crocodile farm is tight, so plan it for a different day.
